---
title: "ML-Accelerated Metadynamics"
subtitle: "Can a pretrained machine-learned potential stand in for a quantum-chemical reference — and where it can't, can we correct it without retraining?"
toc: false
---

The long-term goal is a workflow where enhanced sampling runs on a **machine-learned
surrogate** at the accuracy of the underlying quantum-chemical reference. Getting
there means answering four questions in order: does an off-the-shelf potential agree
with the reference at equilibrium, does that agreement survive bond breaking, can a
lightweight correction close the gap that appears, and does that correction keep
improving when fed more data.

Each pillar below is a 2–4 minute read. The detailed **Studies** remain the source of
truth for methodology, full tables, convergence tests, and troubleshooting.

::: {.pillar-grid}

::: {.pillar-card}
[PILLAR 1]{.num}

### [MACE ↔ xTB validation](p1-validation.qmd)

[Does off-the-shelf MACE-OFF23 reproduce GFN2-xTB for equilibrium water?]{.q}

[**Yes.** Forces correlate at r ≈ 0.99 and MD reproduces droplet structure.]{.hit}
:::

::: {.pillar-card .flagship}
[PILLAR 2]{.num}

### [Reactive chemistry](p2-reactive.qmd)

[Does that agreement survive bond-forming chemistry?]{.q}

[**No.** Barriers differ by ~29 kcal/mol — a genuine difference between the two
potential-energy surfaces, not a path-search artifact.]{.hit}
:::

::: {.pillar-card .flagship}
[PILLAR 3]{.num}

### [Post-training correction](p3-correction.qmd)

[Can a lightweight correction close that gap without touching the foundation model?]{.q}

[**Largely, once.** A targeted conservative Delta puts the certified saddle at
6.33 kcal/mol against an xTB target of 6.7.]{.hit}
:::

::: {.pillar-card}
[PILLAR 4]{.num}

### [Iterative calibration](p4-iterative.qmd)

[Does repeating that correction with more targeted data keep improving it?]{.q}

[**No.** 42 further reference calculations did not improve on iteration 0 — a
useful negative result.]{.hit}
:::

:::

## The scientific chain

Each pillar exists because the previous one produced a specific question:

1. **Equilibrium agreement is strong** — which makes the reactive test meaningful
   rather than a foregone conclusion.
2. **Reactive agreement fails, and the failure is localized** to the transition-state
   region — which motivates correcting *there* rather than globally.
3. **Targeted correction works, once** — which raises the obvious follow-up: does it
   keep working if iterated?
4. **It does not** — which points at correction capacity, not reference-data quantity,
   as the next thing to test.

The [Research Map](research-map.qmd) shows how the individual studies attach to this
chain. It is optional — everything on the main pages stands on its own.

## Results at a glance

| # | Study | Headline result | Pillar |
|---|-------|-----------------|:---:|
| 01 | [Bias × size](01-sweep.qmd) | The RMSD bias breaks the **weakest** bond; small clusters evaporate. | [1](p1-validation.qmd) |
| 02 | [PBC & temperature](02-pbc.qmd) | Periodicity confines the system; a large O–O gap is *drift*, not dissociation. | [1](p1-validation.qmd) |
| 03 | [Droplets](03-droplets.qmd) | **Size suppresses evaporation**; raising `kpush` barely perturbs n=20–50. | [1](p1-validation.qmd) |
| 04 | [Diels–Alder](04-diels-alder.qmd) | Verified concerted TS at **6.7 kcal/mol**, −394 cm⁻¹; raw MACE gives ~36. | [2](p2-reactive.qmd) |
| 05 | [MACE-OFF23](05-mace.qmd) | Forces track xTB at **r ≈ 0.99**; MD structure reproduced; crossover by n≈50. | [1](p1-validation.qmd) |
| 06 | [kpush scaling](06-kpush.qmd) | Bias force ∝ **kpush/N**, so `kpush` must scale ∝ N. | [1](p1-validation.qmd) |
| 07 | [CV design](07-cv-design.qmd) | 7 candidate CVs collapse to ~3 independent axes. | [1](p1-validation.qmd) |
| 08 | [Corrections](08-corrections.qmd) | A conservative pairwise **Delta** removes most of the barrier error; iterating it does not help further. | [3](p3-correction.qmd) · [4](p4-iterative.qmd) |

## Methods in one paragraph

Gas-phase and periodic **GFN2/GFN1-xTB** metadynamics (built-in Cartesian-RMSD bias),
NVT, 0.5 fs timestep; analysis with ASE / NumPy / pandas. Reactions via `xtb --path`,
relaxed concerted scans, and **Sella** saddle optimization with Hessian verification.
Surrogate benchmarking with **MACE-OFF23 (small)** as an ASE calculator; corrections
applied through a `CorrectedCalculator` wrapper so the foundation model is never
modified. All code, data, and figures are in the
[repository](https://github.com/tiangroup-uofa/xtb_metadynamics); each study page links
to its detailed `FINDINGS` document.

::: {.methodnote}
[On the RMSD bias]{.lbl}
xTB biases along **Cartesian RMSD** to previously visited structures — not along any
bond or angle. Every collective variable computed in analysis is a *post-hoc
descriptor*, and `Epot` versus a CV is a **sampled potential-energy landscape from a
biased run**, not a free-energy surface.
:::
